documents.name: Sukagawa Tokusatsu Archives Center
documents.localName: 須賀川特撮アーカイブセンター
documents.summary: A municipal preservation centre where real tokusatsu production miniatures, props and effects artefacts make Japan's practical-effects craft visible at close range.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare, concentrated look at the physical production culture behind Japanese tokusatsu; for practical-effects enthusiasts it offers material that is difficult to encounter in ordinary film or pop-culture museums.

booking.note: Individual visitors do not need reservations; groups of ten or more should contact the centre.

coreExperience.note: Production artefacts are visually legible, but detailed archival interpretation is Japanese-first.

digital.note: Sukagawa City maintains English visitor/logistics information.

coreExperience.note: Machine translation can recover label context, though specialist archival detail is richer in Japanese.

mobility.note: Municipal visitor information documents elevator and wheelchair-accessible facilities.

photography.label: Photography is restricted
photography.note: Check the current municipal rules before shooting; video, flash/tripods and some camera use are restricted.

documents.name: Bannai Shokudo
documents.summary: A benchmark for Kitakata’s clear, pork-forward ramen and the city’s early-morning ramen culture.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Despite fame and queues, the bowl remains a useful reference point for the regional style rather than a celebrity stop detached from its food.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Early opening and sell-out/closing patterns should be checked on the official site.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; weekday mornings give the best experience.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited but the menu is simple.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required due to queue procedure.

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible from Kitakata Station but not immediate

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Mutsu Minato Station Morning Market
documents.summary: The market turns a working port's seafood distribution culture into a self-assembled breakfast without reducing it to one tourist restaurant.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Port-market breakfast assembled from independent vendors. The recommended visit is: Arrive early, buy rice and soup, then compose breakfast from several vendors.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Very early morning; many stalls finish by late morning and market days vary.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday early morning; avoid arriving near closing

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited; vendor communication is mainly Japanese

legacy-car-usefulness.label: Car usefulness
legacy-car-usefulness.note: Useful for combining with coast/port visits

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Food is bought from separate vendors; seating and cleanup rules should be observed.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Mostly cash is safest; current cashless acceptance varies by stall

documents.name: Misawa Aviation & Science Museum
documents.localName: 青森県立三沢航空科学館
documents.summary: A large aviation-and-science museum where real aircraft and unusually tactile flight exhibits make the engineering legible rather than merely display it.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Very good regional destination for aviation, engineering and hands-on science; worth a meaningful detour in northern Aomori, especially for families. Adults uninterested in aircraft will get less from the trip.

audience.notes: Best from preschool age upward; school-age children can engage with the widest range of interactive science content.

coverImage.alt: Aircraft at Misawa Aviation & Science Museum in Aomori.

documents.name: Tadami Megumi-no-Mori
documents.summary: A beech-forest river corridor is experienced from inside the shallow stream itself, with repeated crossings, clear pools and small falls rather than a conventional dry trail.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The unusual relationship between forest and river makes the route much more than an approach to a named waterfall. In safe water it is one of the research run's clearest examples of an obscure E4-quality landscape.

documents.name: Toyosu Tuna Auction Observation
documents.localName: 豊洲市場 マグロせり見学
documents.summary: An early-morning viewing opportunity for Toyosu’s working tuna auction, including a lottery-controlled observation deck for the closest public view.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It offers a rare glimpse into the wholesale system behind a globally important part of Japanese food culture and works well as a specialist early-morning component.

booking.note: Booking depends on the selected programme, viewing area or guided component; verify the current arrangement.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The experience is brief and observational, the best deck is lottery-dependent and the early start creates disproportionate logistical friction.

visit-window.note: Market operating days and auction-viewing procedures must be checked before an early-morning trip.

documents.name: Awaji Tadao Ando Architecture Circuit
documents.localName: 淡路島 安藤忠雄建築
documents.summary: A concentrated Awaji Island architecture circuit linking Tadao Ando’s vast Yumebutai landscape complex with the compact, intensely staged Honpukuji Water Temple.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The island lets architecture-focused visitors experience Ando’s concrete, water, light and landscape language across two genuinely different spatial scales in one coherent half- to full-day circuit.

booking.note: The two principal public sites do not form one reserved tour; verify current opening hours separately before building the circuit.

coreExperience.note: The core architectural experience is spatial and visual; Japanese is not required to appreciate either principal work.

mobility.note: Yumebutai is a large terraced landscape complex with extensive vertical circulation; visitors should not infer a compact two-building stop from the map.

multi-site.label: Two-site architecture circuit
multi-site.note: The MultiPoint geometry deliberately represents Yumebutai and Honpukuji Water Temple; transport between them is part of the visit.

weather.condition: Allow for substantial outdoor circulation at Yumebutai.
weather.note: The architecture is visitable year-round, but rain, summer heat and strong weather change the comfort of the landscape-heavy Yumebutai component.

documents.name: Ikaho Toy, Doll and Car Museum
documents.localName: 伊香保おもちゃと人形自動車博物館
documents.summary: A sprawling private collection that unfolds from Showa streets and toys into classic cars, retro games, popular-culture rooms and an Initial D reconstruction, far larger and stranger than its roadside exterior suggests.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It satisfies the seed's appetite for dense discovery and obsessive curation through a different medium: the pleasure is opening one improbable room after another and encountering the material culture surrounding Japanese childhood, cars and entertainment.

coreExperience.note: The visual collection is accessible without Japanese, while deeper labels and nostalgic references are Japanese-first.
Camera translation adds context but is not required to enjoy the objects and environments.

mobility.note: The one-way multi-level route uses many stairs and has no elevator according to current specialist family guidance.

allow-time.label: Allow at least two hours
allow-time.note: The route is much larger than the exterior suggests and cannot be easily shortened or backtracked.

verify-current-info.label: Verify current hours, price and activities
verify-current-info.note: Current secondary listings conflict and individual participatory activities change.

documents.name: Kitayamazaki Coast Trail
documents.summary: The worthwhile version of famous Kitayamazaki is a strenuous trail through forest, fishing settlements, stairs and 200 m-class sea cliffs rather than a drive-up lookout.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Walking converts a famous static panorama into one of the strongest under-recognized mainland sea-cliff journeys found in the research. The sustained physical relationship with the coast is the reason to allocate a full day or two.

coverImage.alt: Steep forested sea cliffs and offshore rock stacks along the Kitayamazaki coast.

documents.name: Nakatanidou
documents.summary: Central Nara sweets shop famous for fresh mugwort mochi and rapid public mochi-pounding demonstrations.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Fresh yomogi mochi plus high-speed pounding demonstrations combine excellent value with public craft spectacle.

documents.name: Shima Spain Village Parque España
documents.localName: 志摩スペイン村 パルケエスパーニャ
documents.summary: A remote, unusually committed Spanish-themed park whose walkable streets, live parade and flamenco, architecture, food and often relaxed crowd levels turn an improbable premise into a cult full-day experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The park's strength is not maximum ride intensity but a coherent place with human-scale performance and room to notice craft. That reality-beats-premise pattern, sustained by repeat-fan behaviour, supports A for themed-environment travellers; remoteness, weather and date-dependent show energy keep confidence medium.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: Immersive themed village and performance park

booking.note: Advance purchase is useful, but the more important step is checking the operating calendar and show schedule.

duration.note: Treat it as a full day, especially when the parade and flamenco or show schedule is operating.

mobility.note: The park is large and partly hilly but uses normal theme-park paths; consult current attraction restrictions and mobility services for individual needs.

documents.name: Universal Studios Japan
documents.localName: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
documents.summary: Japan’s major Universal park, combining Super Nintendo World, Wizarding World, high-intensity rides and rotating Japanese IP events in a dense full-day product.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The best lands and rides repeatedly produce exceptional visitor reactions and the park has enough breadth for a deliberate Osaka itinerary day, but capacity pressure and paid queue-management complexity materially reduce reliability.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: destination theme park · immersive themed lands

documents.name: Yokkaichi Industrial Night Cruise
documents.localName: 四日市コンビナート夜景クルーズ
documents.summary: A close water-level night cruise through Yokkaichi’s refinery and petrochemical landscape of pipes, tanks, loading structures and flare stacks.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The moving harbour perspective gives operating industrial infrastructure an unusual cinematic scale and works as a strong evening component around Nagoya or Mie, but sailing/time selection matters enough to keep it at B.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: industrial night cruise · working port landscape

booking.note: Reserve the specific sailing in advance.

coreExperience.note: Guide narration adds context, but the visual industrial landscape is the core product.

mobility.note: Physical effort is low, but some sailings may require prolonged standing on a moving vessel because seating is limited.

seating.label: Do not assume a seated night-view experience
seating.note: Recent visitor reviews report limited seating and occasional crowding/sightline problems.

weather.label: Dress for an exposed night cruise
weather.note: A 2025 winter report describes spending the full hour outside and needing serious cold protection.

darkness.condition: Choose a sailing that reaches the industrial waterfront after full darkness.
darkness.note: Recent summer complaints show that an early departure can consume much of the cruise before the nightscape is actually dark.

documents.name: Oga Shinzan Folklore Museum
documents.summary: An intimate live recreation of Oga's Namahage New Year house visit inside a traditional magariya, best paired with the adjacent museum's extraordinary regional mask collection.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The small scale is a strength: proximity, sound, movement and ritual dialogue create a concentrated encounter that a static folklore display cannot. Regional specificity, the paired mask collection and recurring strong reactions support A; remoteness, schedule dependence and language or sensory friction prevent S.

booking.note: Individuals generally use scheduled sessions; groups may require advance arrangements. Confirm current performance times before travelling.

duration.note: Allow about 2 hours for the scheduled demonstration and the adjacent Namahage Museum.

mobility.note: The traditional building and performance setting may have thresholds or seating constraints; contact the facility for current mobility arrangements. Loud sound and masked performers are sensory considerations.

documents.name: Ek Chuah Karahori “Kura” Main Shop
documents.localName: エクチュア からほり「蔵」本店
documents.summary: Long-running chocolatier and cafe inside a renovated historic storehouse in the Karahori district.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong chocolate-focused cafe food in a historic Karahori storehouse, backed by substantial diner evidence.

documents.name: Hayashiya Nakanoso
documents.summary: Unpretentious Nakano yoshoku restaurant specialising in hayashi rice, omelettes, curry and meat-sauce pasta.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A durable, unpretentious yoshoku specialist where omu-hayashi is a particularly coherent order.

documents.name: Koiwai Farm Makiba-en
documents.summary: A destination-scale working-farm visitor park mixing animals, pasture recreation, tractor rides, food production, heritage interpretation and hands-on making.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very good rural family destination and worthwhile regional detour in Iwate, particularly in good weather. Much of the appeal is outdoors and seasonal; individual paid activities and same-day capacities can shape the visit.

audience.notes: Broad family fit, with some workshops or rides carrying their own minimum ages or supervision requirements.

coverImage.alt: Entrance gate of Koiwai Farm Makiba-en in Iwate.

documents.name: Oze National Park Wetlands
documents.summary: A vast high-elevation marshland landscape crossed by boardwalks, ringed by mountains and transformed by seasonal flowers and autumn colour.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The broad open wetlands, reflective pools and long boardwalk journey create a distinctive landscape experience unlike Japan’s more typical forest or summit hikes.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Peak seasons bring crowds, access is bus-and-trailhead dependent and weather can turn an easy boardwalk day into a wet, cold outing.

visit-window.note: The accessible hiking season is strongly seasonal; snow closure, flowers and autumn colour change the value of a visit.

documents.name: Kozagawa River Corridor
documents.summary: A clear-water river journey linking a giant monolith, dense pothole fields, low submersible bridges and forested valley scenery.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong regional discovery because the pieces reinforce each other, but not worth a cross-country journey for one roadside stop alone. Visit in dry stable weather when the river is clear; post-rain turbidity weakens much of the visual appeal.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Half or full day by car; kayaking is optional and dependent on water and operator conditions.

coverImage.alt: The enormous Ichimai-iwa rock wall rising beside the Kozagawa River.

documents.name: Tokyo Skytree
documents.summary: Tokyo’s 634 m broadcast tower with public decks at 350 m and 450 m, offering the city’s highest mainstream panorama and a glass spiral through the Tembo Galleria.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The sheer height produces a genuinely distinctive geographic reading of Tokyo, but current visitor evidence shows crowding, haze and weak incremental value from the upper deck; it is strong B rather than the city’s best observatory.

documents.name: Mitsutaya
documents.summary: An unusually coherent Aizu meal built around skewered tofu, mochi, herring and vegetables grilled over charcoal and brushed with miso.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It compresses several Aizu food traditions into one focused, affordable experience with a strong sense of place.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Check current closing days; heritage building and charcoal service limit throughput.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round, especially appealing in cool weather.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Manageable with a set menu and translation.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Yanmar Museum
documents.localName: ヤンマーミュージアム
documents.summary: A challenge-based industrial museum where children operate and simulate agricultural, marine and construction machinery instead of only reading about it.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A very good child-centred industrial discovery and a meaningful detour for families in northern Shiga. Reservation priority and time/content limits on busy days matter, and adults visiting without children may find the experience comparatively lightweight.

audience.notes: Designed especially strongly for children; individual challenges have their own minimum ages, size or supervision rules.

coverImage.alt: Exhibition floor inside Yanmar Museum in Nagahama, Shiga.

documents.name: Nakai Shunpudo
documents.summary: The controlled heating and rapid setting of genuine kudzu are demonstrated and tasted at the moment when texture is most expressive.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Transparent preparation of true Yoshino kudzu. The recommended visit is: Reserve or time a preparation-focused tasting and eat immediately; compare texture as it cools.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Small capacity; service may be timed and seasonal.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cooler quiet day, paired with Yoshino visit

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Made-to-order product has a very short optimal eating window; punctuality matters.

documents.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge World
documents.localName: 明石海峡大橋塔頂体験ブリッジワールド
documents.summary: A nearly three-hour guided engineering tour through normally closed Akashi Kaikyo Bridge maintenance space, across a grated sea-level walkway and up to the roughly 300 m tower top.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare chance to experience a famous structure from inside its working maintenance system rather than simply view it from shore.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: bridge engineering tour · restricted infrastructure access

booking.note: Tours are advance-reservation, first-come and operate on designated dates.

coreExperience.note: The engineering explanation is guide-led in Japanese.

safety.note: Participants must understand or reliably translate safety instructions.

mobility.note: Participants must independently walk more than 2 km and climb stairs.

height.label: Not suitable for severe fear of heights or enclosed spaces
height.note: Participation rules explicitly exclude visitors with serious height or claustrophobia concerns.

coverImage.alt: Grated maintenance walkway used by the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge World tour.

documents.name: Mozumo
documents.summary: A small Hirayu retreat where reliable kakenagashi, snow and forest immersion matter more than luxury branding.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A small Hirayu retreat where reliable kakenagashi, snow and forest immersion matter more than luxury branding.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥80,000–120,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Baths can be compact for two and the property is not detached.

documents.name: Spa Resort Hawaiians
documents.localName: スパリゾートハワイアンズ
documents.summary: A genuinely destination-scale indoor aquatic resort combining big pools and slides, child water zones, hot-water bathing and permanent Polynesian stage entertainment.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major regional destination and one of Japan’s most substantial all-weather aquatic attractions. Summer and holiday crowds, swim logistics and extra-charge activities can materially affect value, but the breadth justifies a dedicated visit for water-loving families and adults.

audience.notes: Very broad family appeal, but individual slides and activities have their own height or participation rules that should be checked before visiting.

coverImage.alt: Indoor water park at Spa Resort Hawaiians in Iwaki, Fukushima.

documents.name: Azumaya Honten
documents.summary: The value is not merely eating soba but participating in a codified, server-led meal format that remains one of Morioka's defining food customs.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Morioka's competitive/ceremonial continuously served soba format. The recommended visit is: Choose the full wanko format rather than an ordinary soba bowl if this is a deliberate visit.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Current reception hours and wanko cutoff should be checked; groups may require booking.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Lunch on a non-holiday weekday

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some multilingual guidance is commonly available; verify

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: B: ritual needs explanation but staff routinely handle visitors

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Online or phone depending on plan

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Follow the server's pace and closing-bowl signal; one-order-per-participant conditions may apply.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Cards likely accepted; verify current branch policy

documents.name: Ashikaga Flower Park at Peak Wisteria
documents.localName: あしかがフラワーパーク 大藤
documents.summary: A seasonal garden whose mature wisteria canopies form enormous curtains and tunnels of flowers, with evening illumination during the peak festival.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At peak bloom the scale and age of the principal wisteria create a destination-grade botanical spectacle rather than an ordinary flower garden.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The A-tier case is tightly bloom-dependent; peak weeks are crowded and an off-peak visit is a materially weaker experience.

visit-window.note: Target peak wisteria, usually late April into early May; bloom timing shifts with weather.

documents.name: Daiwa Sushi
documents.summary: A high-signal Toyosu breakfast counter where repeated diners return for fast, generous market sushi and where arriving at dawn can turn a famous queue into a compact, memorable meal.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A-tier: unusually strong repeat behavior from domestic diners plus current destination-level praise from international visitors make Daiwa worth a Toyosu detour; it stops short of S because Sushi Dai and other market counters provide credible alternatives and queue/price friction is material.

customFacets.food.destinationWorthiness: Worth a deliberate Toyosu detour, particularly when combined with the market.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Roughly ¥6,000–14,000 depending on set and additions

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Closed Sundays, national holidays and Toyosu Market closure days; check the current market calendar.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; very early morning is the key timing variable.

legacy-availability-conditions.label: Availability conditions
legacy-availability-conditions.note: Walk-in only; closes around early afternoon and can sell out or stop accepting customers earlier.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Formal English-menu coverage is inconsistent, but current visitor reports describe some staff English/Chinese communication.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Low to moderate if ordering the standard chef's set; detailed fish explanations can be language-dependent.

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Strong: Shijo-mae Station is adjacent, though internal wayfinding to the 5-block fruit-and-vegetable building can confuse first-time visitors.

legacy-car-usefulness.label: Car usefulness
legacy-car-usefulness.note: Low; the market is designed for public-transport access and general visitor parking is constrained.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Do not obstruct market operations; queue compactly and expect an efficient counter meal.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Current platform data indicates cards/contactless are accepted; carry a backup payment method.

documents.name: Kadocho Soy Sauce Museum and Shokunin-gura
documents.localName: 角長 醤油資料館・職人蔵
documents.summary: The small buildings make soy-sauce brewing legible inside the townscape that claims a foundational role in Japanese shoyu history.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Traditional Yuasa soy-sauce brewing and townscape. The recommended visit is: Visit both interpretive spaces, then taste the flagship naturally brewed soy sauce in a simple use.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Museum opening days and actual production access differ; verify.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cool weekday morning

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Rail access possible, but car helps wider area

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Production areas beyond public museum are restricted.

documents.name: Arayo Main Store and Fugu-Ovary Fermentation Workshop
documents.localName: あら与 本店・ふぐの子発酵体験
documents.summary: One of the rare lawful places to observe and finish-taste long-fermented pufferfish ovaries, a food tradition that appears impossible until its multi-year detoxification is understood.
documents.whyWorthwhile: This is among the catalogue’s most singular fermentation experiences—technically, historically and sensorially difficult to substitute anywhere else.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Full programme excludes July, August and December and is subject to producer availability; participants must be at least 18.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Spring, autumn or early winter outside excluded months; book well ahead.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: No English programme confirmed; arrange a Japanese-speaking helper or robust live translation.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required; the booking and technical explanation are Japanese-led.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Required at least two weeks ahead

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Book through the current Hakusan experience programme/direct organiser; 2–5 adults

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible by rail/taxi but a car simplifies the industrial-neighbourhood visit

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Participants must meet the published age and group-size limits; follow all hygiene instructions and do not treat unprocessed material as edible.

documents.name: Atsuta Horaiken Honten
documents.localName: あつた蓬莱軒 本店
documents.summary: The meal's sequence—plain, condiments, then dashi—makes hitsumabushi a format rather than simply another eel bowl.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Layered eel-rice eating format associated with Nagoya. The recommended visit is: Order one standard hitsumabushi per diner and follow the three-stage eating sequence.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Very high demand; service and ticketing can stop before nominal closing.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday before opening or off-peak

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Current queue-registration and reservation policy must be checked

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Queue registration and return-time rules may apply; do not assume walk-up immediate seating.

documents.name: Wonderia Yokohama
documents.summary: A polished indoor nature-discovery attraction built around six projection-led environments and app-linked exploration.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is an easy, well-produced Yokohama family experience with enough interactive discovery to outperform a simple projection exhibition.

booking.note: Advance planning is useful on busy weekends and holidays; this is a capacity issue, not a seasonal one.

coreExperience.note: The visual environments remain usable without fluent Japanese, while app/discovery detail benefits from translation.

mobility.note: Compact indoor attraction; no unusual physical demand was established in this pass.

app-dependence.label: Phone/app use is part of the discovery layer
app-dependence.note: Visitors who avoid app-led interaction will get a thinner experience.

documents.name: Furukawa Festival & Okoshi-daiko
documents.summary: Hida-Furukawa's April festival pairs refined daytime yatai floats and shrine ritual with the forceful night Okoshi-daiko drum procession.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The contrast between refined float culture and muscular night drumming gives compact Hida-Furukawa a distinctive festival identity strong enough for a date-specific detour.

booking.note: General public street viewing is not a ticketed attraction; transport/accommodation on the two festival days should be planned early.

coreExperience.note: Float movement, drumming and street ritual are visually legible; Japanese adds ceremonial context.

mobility.note: Seeing both yatai and the night drum means hours of walking/standing in Furukawa's compact streets.

late-night-weather.label: Prepare for a long spring evening outdoors
late-night-weather.note: The night procession runs late; use weather-appropriate layers and comfortable standing/walking footwear.

festival-window.condition: Travel for the fixed April 19–20 programme and confirm current weather/event notices.
festival-window.note: The headline Okoshi-daiko is tied to the first night; weather can alter associated programme elements.

documents.name: Hitachi Furyumono
documents.summary: A roughly 15-metre festival float that opens into a five-level karakuri puppet stage; one district normally performs at the annual Sakura Festival, while all four floats assemble only for the rare Kamine Shrine Grand Festival.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Even the normal rotating annual float offers a highly unusual combination of monumental engineering and live karakuri theatre, while the rare all-four gathering substantially raises the ceiling for festival specialists.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: mechanical float performance · karakuri puppet theatre

booking.note: Normal street viewing is not a reserved attraction; follow the current festival traffic/viewing plan.

coreExperience.note: The mechanical transformation and puppetry are strongly visual; Japanese adds story and ritual context.

documents.name: Museum Meiji-Mura
documents.summary: A vast open-air architectural village where more than 60 relocated Meiji-period buildings, working steam transport and lived-in interiors turn modernization history into a full-day walk through another era.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of architectural authenticity, breadth, inhabitable interiors, landscape and operating steam and street transport produces unusually convincing historical time travel. Its size, hills, heat and interpretation unevenness are substantial planning constraints rather than defects in the core experience.

documents.name: Saku Hotel
documents.summary: The hotel is a potential window into a regional freshwater-fish tradition that is otherwise easy to overlook, especially carp preparation in inland Nagano.

documents.summary: A rare Gero stay where registered 1931 architecture, forested hillside rooms and source-fed private baths reinforce one another instead of competing as separate attractions.

documents.summary: A Mount Rokko museum and sound garden where antique automatic instruments still perform, technicians preserve their mechanisms and visitors can extend the experience by winding outdoor sound boxes or assembling a music box.

documents.localName: レーヴ・デ・リュミエール
documents.summary: A dedicated 1,500 m² immersive-art venue in Ariake using large-scale projection and spatial audio for rotating artist programmes.

documents.name: Antarctic Research Ship Fuji
documents.summary: A preserved Japanese Antarctic research ship at Nagoya Port whose cabins, work spaces, helicopter and expedition exhibits can be explored in the vessel itself.

documents.localName: 獅子ヶ鼻湿原・中島台

documents.name: Game Center Mikado Takadanobaba
documents.localName: 高田馬場ゲーセンミカド
documents.summary: A living old-school Japanese video arcade where rare cabinets, fighting and shooting games are still meant to be played, and regular tournaments preserve the social culture around them.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A strong Tokyo recommendation for anyone who cares about arcade history or Japanese competitive-game culture, and a much more authentic play experience than a display-only retro-game exhibit.

documents.name: JAL Sky Museum
documents.summary: A free reservation-only JAL museum and maintenance-hangar tour offering real operational aircraft access at Haneda.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Seeing active maintenance close-up gives aviation enthusiasts a level of operational reality that conventional transport museums cannot match.

documents.name: Chichibu Night Festival
documents.summary: One of Japan’s major float festivals, culminating in illuminated ornate floats hauled through Chichibu alongside a large winter fireworks programme.

documents.name: PokéPark Kanto
documents.localName: ポケパーク カントー
documents.summary: A permanent Pokémon environment inside Yomiuriland, combining a steep 500-metre Pokémon Forest discovery trail with the more accessible Sedge Town of shops, encounters and themed streets.
documents.whyWorthwhile: PokéPark Kanto converts collection and observation—the franchise's core pleasures—into a physical discovery walk rather than a conventional ride park. The new attraction's short operating history, price, steep route and exclusionary forest rules make B the defensible current tier.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: Pokémon discovery world and forest trail

booking.note: A dated ticket is required. Japan residents use the official lottery/first-come sales system; visitors residing outside Japan are directed to the operator-authorized English ticket store. Buy well ahead because capacity and ticket products are controlled.

duration.note: Allow about 4 hours; ticket type, photography pace and town queues can extend the visit.

mobility.note: Pokémon Forest uses steep natural terrain and a 110-step staircase; visitors who cannot safely climb the staircase independently are restricted from the full route, and children under 5 and their guardians cannot enter. The operator now documents stairlift-assisted wheelchair access to a relatively gently sloped area from the Forest entrance. Sedge Town remains the practical alternative for visitors who cannot use the Forest route.

constraint.note: The strongest experience depends on the chosen guide and itinerary; access rules, reconstruction and language support change.

visit-window.condition: Book a current guided programme rather than relying on a historical route.
visit-window.note: Programmes operate on scheduled dates and access can change with reconstruction work.

documents.name: Sawara Grand Festival
documents.summary: Tall doll-topped floats move through Sawara's preserved canal-town streets with music, tight turns and neighbourhood ritual during separate summer and autumn festivals.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of large traditional floats and one of Kanto's strongest preserved merchant-town settings creates a coherent festival destination rather than an isolated parade.

booking.note: General street viewing is not a ticketed attraction; accommodation and transport on peak dates may still reward advance planning.

coreExperience.note: Float movement, music and the historic streetscape are visually legible without Japanese; language adds ritual and neighbourhood context.

mobility.note: A strong visit involves walking the historic district and prolonged street viewing rather than staying at one fixed seat.

crowds-weather.label: Prepare for crowds and outdoor weather
crowds-weather.note: Comfortable walking footwear and rain/sun protection matter during a multi-hour historic-district festival visit.

festival-calendar.condition: Choose the summer or autumn festival and verify that year's exact programme.
festival-calendar.note: Sawara Grand Festival is not one continuous event; the two annual festivals use separate dates and neighbourhood floats.

weather.condition: Rain changes comfort and can alter the street experience.
weather.note: Recent visitors deliberately planned around rain forecasts; the event remains an outdoor walking/standing day.

documents.name: Tokyo Tower
documents.summary: Tokyo’s 333-metre red-and-white landmark with a 150 m Main Deck and a guided/timed 250 m Top Deck sequence, combining a close-grained city view with the physical tower structure.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It remains more than an icon because the lower-height city detail, exposed steel and historical identity give it a different experience from Skytree, though the cramped Top Deck and elevator queues keep it below A.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: urban observation tower · historic broadcast tower

documents.name: RENEW
documents.summary: An annual open-factory festival across Fukui craft districts, turning workshops and normally closed production spaces into a region-wide visitor route.
documents.whyWorthwhile: RENEW reveals lacquerware, eyewear, knives, textiles and other craft industries as active production systems through direct workshop access and conversation rather than finished objects in a museum.

booking.note: Open workshops vary, while limited hands-on experiences can fill early; reserve high-priority activities before travel.

coreExperience.note: Direct conversation with makers is a major part of the value; Japanese or effective translation materially improves the visit.

mobility.note: Selected districts can be explored heavily on foot; covering distant districts requires additional transport.

multi-site.label: Do not attempt to cover the whole festival
multi-site.note: A recent three-day visitor cut a four-area plan down to two and explicitly recommends focusing on one or two districts.

walking-prep.label: Comfortable walking shoes and sun protection
walking-prep.note: Recent participant advice specifically calls out walking shoes, hat/sunglasses and early reservations.

annual-programme.condition: Use the current RENEW map and choose one or two districts before arrival.
annual-programme.note: Participants and bookable workshop experiences change each year.

documents.name: Hachinohe Sansha Taisai
documents.summary: A five-day summer festival built around enormous mechanically transforming floats, shrine processions and city-wide evening spectacle.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The scale, density and engineering of the floats make Hachinohe one of Tohoku’s strongest urban festival experiences rather than a generic parade.

booking.note: Public street viewing does not inherently require booking; reserved viewing products and peak accommodation should be planned separately.

coreExperience.note: The floats and processions are visually immediate; Japanese adds shrine and neighbourhood context.

mobility.note: Good viewing often requires walking along or repositioning around the procession route and prolonged standing.

summer-weather.label: Prepare for summer heat and rain
summer-weather.note: First-hand reporting documents heavy rain during the procession; hot weather is also a normal August concern.

visit-window.condition: Choose the festival day and procession/viewing area deliberately.
visit-window.note: The five-day programme has different procession and evening components around July 31–August 4.

documents.name: Tsugaru Akatsuki no Kai
documents.summary: This is one of the clearest visitor pathways into dishes that otherwise survive inside homes, seasonal labour and communal memory rather than restaurants.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Tsugaru household and ceremonial cooking transmitted by a women's group. The recommended visit is: Book the complete group meal and ask in advance which seasonal dishes will appear.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Advance booking is required; prior material specified at least four days and a minimum group size of four, but reconfirm.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Autumn and winter for preservation foods; any confirmed seasonal meal

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: D: advance Japanese coordination is realistically needed

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Advance contact; Japanese assistance strongly recommended

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible within Hirosaki, but exact meeting logistics require preparation

legacy-car-usefulness.label: Car usefulness
legacy-car-usefulness.note: Useful; venue logistics should be confirmed

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Group minimum and advance-booking conditions apply; do not arrive unannounced.

documents.name: CURE MAID CAFÉ
documents.summary: A long-running Akihabara maid café whose point is the opposite of theatrical 'moe' spectacle: classical uniforms, calm service, tea and ordinary café use.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Visit it as a subculture-history experience and a counterpoint to theatrical maid cafés: the continuity of the restrained service style is more interesting than treating it as another themed restaurant.

booking.note: Ordinary visits are generally walk-in; crowded periods may use numbered tickets and reservations are restricted.

coreExperience.note: The core is an ordinary café/service interaction, but stable English menu/service support was not verified.
Machine translation is practical for menu/detail gaps.

mobility.note: Ordinary seated café visit; building step-free details should be checked if essential.

expectations.label: This is the restrained maid-café format
expectations.note: Do not choose CURE if the goal is chants, games or theatrical maid performance.

photography.label: Follow staff-safe photography rules
photography.note: Still photography is conditional; do not include staff or other customers, and video is not allowed.

documents.name: Sumaura Yuen
documents.summary: A deliberately old-fashioned hillside amusement park reached by ropeway, centred on Japan’s surviving Carlator conveyor ride, a rotating observatory and a chairlift across the ridge.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Carlator is not a one-photo gimmick: stacked vintage transport modes, mechanical eccentricity and a strong Kobe/Seto Inland Sea viewpoint make a coherent two-hour retro experience worth a local detour.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: vintage hillside amusement park · ropeway and Carlator ride

documents.name: arcana izu
documents.summary: Destination cuisine and a river-forest bath create one of the best food-plus-onsen experiences in Japan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Destination cuisine and a river-forest bath create one of the best food-plus-onsen experiences in Japan.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥119,000–194,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor source bath is guaranteed in every suite.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Water-treatment detail is not as explicit as the kakenagashi leaders and pricing is high.

documents.name: Europe-ken Main Store
documents.localName: ヨーロッパ軒 総本店
documents.summary: The canonical reference for Fukui’s sauce katsudon: thin pork cutlets dipped in a tangy Worcestershire-style sauce.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is affordable, specific and culturally useful, though not worth an extreme detour for diners indifferent to fried pork.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Confirm main-store closing day and branch-specific menu.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Mikimoto Pearl Island & Ama-Hut Experience
documents.localName: ミキモト真珠島・海女小屋体験
documents.summary: A bookable five-hour guided Toba day tour pairing Mikimoto Pearl Island’s pearl-cultivation history and ama demonstration with an active-ama seafood lunch in Osatsu.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The exact guided sequence connects the historical role of ama in cultured-pearl production with a present-day Osatsu community encounter, making the day more coherent than treating either component in isolation.

booking.note: Book by 16:00 on the preceding day. The operator lists a 1–5 person tour size and may cancel if minimum participation is not reached.

coreExperience.note: The product is a visitor-facing guided tour and direct international visitor evidence confirms usable interpretation.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: This is a relatively expensive fixed guided day and may be cancelled for stormy weather or insufficient participation; Mikimoto’s ama segment is a demonstration, while the Osatsu lunch supplies the living-culture interaction.

visit-window.condition: Check current tour dates before travel.
visit-window.note: The tour is generally offered year-round but is unavailable in July–August, 29 December–3 January and during Mikimoto Pearl Island closure days.
